subject: Performance SLO - Private VPC qualification (network path, streaming, concurrency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO - Private VPC qualification (network path, streaming, concurrency)

Hi Samir - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can move toward a short PoC for Private/VPC deployment.

Key performance targets you mentioned:
- Latency: target p95 generation latency <= 100ms (token stream) for 512-token seqs; tail latency sensitivity is high.
- Throughput: baseline 200 qps sustained with peaks to 600 qps during batch windows.
- Concurrency: up to ~1200 concurrent short requests (avg payload 40 tokens) across services.
- Streaming: you require token-by-token SSE-style streaming to the client; cannot buffer entire response server-side.

Network/VPC / connectivity notes:
- Preference: AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering (you mentioned Transit Gateway as fallback).
- Egress: you would like minimal public egress; any outbound to Redwoods control plane (for billing/metrics) should be over private endpoints if possible.
- Internal latency budgets: app -> inference cluster (one-way) < 15ms target; jitter < 10ms during peak.
- NAT/Proxies: confirm whether you have outbound proxies that rewrite TLS; we may need certs for mTLS.

Action items we need from Acme to size and validate: (please provide where available)
1) Network diagram including VPC CIDRs, peering/transit gateway topology, and any firewalls/NAT/proxy hops. (attachment preferred)
2) Expected source IP ranges and any allowed ports (we typically need 443 + health check ports 8000-8100 for the PoC).
3) Typical request payload sizes (avg and 95th token counts) and any binary attachments that will be passed.
4) Expected steady-state qps/concurrent calls (you gave ranges above - please confirm weekly variation).
5) Whether PrivateLink is preferred over peering and any procurement/security blockers.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Priya (network lead) will map required ports and CIDR allowances for peering/PrivateLink.
- Jordan will coordinate a short tech sync (30-45m) with your CloudOps + network owner to confirm VPN/peering details and test windows.
- We can provide a temporary test endpoint and a lightweight benchmarking script to run from your VPC for RTT/egress checks.

Can you send the network diagram and confirm preferred connectivity option? I'll book the tech sync once we have your network contact.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Gina Torres <gina@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO - Private VPC qualification (network path, streaming, concurrency)

Thanks Marissa - great summary. I've attached our internal network diagram (acme-network-diagram.pdf). A few clarifications:

- Latency: p95 <=100ms is what we'll aim for; critical for our customer-facing chat experience.
- Connectivity: our preferred option is AWS PrivateLink for tighter security controls, but we can do Transit Gateway peering if PrivateLink isn't feasible.
- Egress: we prefer no public internet egress where possible. We run most telemetry to our internal monitoring; if Redwood needs to send metrics to your control plane, PrivateLink would be ideal.
- Proxies: there is an outbound HTTP proxy for some subnets - I'll confirm whether it rewrites TLS.
- Jitter: we can commit to an internal network SLA of < 8ms median, but peaks may hit ~20ms during some windows.

I attached the network diagram and a sample of request size distributions. Our network owner is Gina Torres (cc'd). She can take the tech sync on our side.

Samir
Senior PM, ACME Corp
samir@acme.com | +1 650-555-0199

Attachment: acme-network-diagram.pdf

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO - Private VPC qualification (network path, streaming, concurrency)

Hi Samir - thanks for the diagram, looks helpful. A few network-level asks from our infra team so we can pre-validate before the tech sync:

1) Public/Private IPs: please confirm the VPC CIDR(s) that will peer with Redwood and any NAT ranges.
2) Ports: for the PoC we need to allow outbound connections from your app subnet to our inference subnet on 443 (TLS), plus health ports 8000-8100 for the initial probes. If using PrivateLink, we'll share the ENI IP ranges to allow inbound.
3) MTLS: do you have an internal CA for mTLS or will you accept mutual TLS with Redwood-managed certs?
4) Throughput tests: propose a short window (1 hour) where we run our load generator from a temporary endpoint - pick a low-traffic slot (we suggest Sat 09/18 02:00-03:00 UTC).

If you can confirm CIDRs and whether PrivateLink is doable, I'll produce a short checklist (redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx) with required firewall rules we can drop into your ticketing system.

--
Priya Natarajan
Network & Infra, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
